attrs.evidence: Kernel row L-BYTES-1: 48/48 corpus states satisfy sha256(stateSignature) == semStateId, the compaction boundary is well-formed on all of them (7 compacted to exactly 65 chars, longest uncompacted exactly 80), and equivariance is asserted at the BYTE level — alpha-variants and label permutations produce the identical signature string, which a digest-level check could not distinguish from a canonical form that agrees only after hashing. grid_check v2.13 verifies the shipped vectors engine-free: every signature is re-hashed against its id, every normal-form nf_id is matched against the refinement receipt, and the compaction row's reconstructed pre-compaction string is re-hashed against the emitted compacted signature. Negative battery cases prehash-signature-tampered, prehash-id-resealed, prehash-nfid-unanchored, and prehash-compaction-lie each die on a distinct diagnostic.
attrs.statement: The canonical digest is DEFINED as sha256 of a canonical signature string, and those pre-hash BYTES are a published artifact rather than an internal detail: stateDigest(s) == sha256(stateSignature(s)) through one code path, never two, so a shipped signature cannot drift from the digest it explains. golden_prehash_vectors.json carries the signature strings for every corpus state (initial and normal form) plus the §5 compaction boundary, so a second implementation diffs the STRING and sees where its canonical form diverges instead of only learning that a hash differs.
